newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call rates edge up, seen firm this week.
newsitem.headline: Indian call rates edge up, seen firm this week.

text.p: Indian call money rates opened at 5.50-6.25 percent on Monday compared to the previous close of 5.0-5.50 percent, dealers said.
The firmer call rates resulted from the drain on liquidity due to a series of auctions last week, they said.
The 364-day treasury bill auction on June 4 raised 4.22 billion rupees at a yield of 9.0 percent. The 91-day treasury bill auction on June 6 raised 3.91 billion rupees.
At the maiden auction of 14-day treasury bills, also on June 6, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) accepted 21 bids for 11.14 billion rupees.
Dealers said the call rates are not expected to soften in the first week of the new fortnight unless RBI intervention in the forex market injected fresh liquidity into the system.
"The advance tax flows on June 15 is expected to soak up about 20 billion rupees," said a dealer at a state-run bank.
